questions.question: D1 — Run outside design voices before the review passes? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-outside-voices>

options.label: No — proceed without (recommended)
options.description: Skip Codex + Claude subagent outside pass. Best for this case: it's a scoped settings form update with a complete DESIGN.md; hard-rejection checks apply to marketing surfaces, not OPERATE/settings UI.

options.label: Yes — run Codex + Claude subagent
options.description: Run Codex against OpenAI design hard rules + litmus checks, and a separate Claude subagent for an independent completeness review. Adds time but catches anything a single-model pass misses.

questions.question: D2 — Pass 2: Export pending state is not specified in the plan. What should the user see while the JSON download is being prepared? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-export-pending>

options.label: Disable + spinner (recommended)
options.description: Apply the same DESIGN.md pending pattern used by Save: disable the Export button, show an inline spinner beside “Exporting…”, aria-busy=true. Reuses existing component behavior; prevents duplicate downloads; consistent with Save pending UX. (human: ~30min / CC: ~5min)

options.label: Disable only, no spinner
options.description: Disable the Export button while downloading but show no spinner. Prevents double-clicks but gives no progress signal. Simpler, but inconsistent with Save pending pattern; user may think it froze. (human: ~15min / CC: ~3min)

options.label: Leave unspecified — implementer decides
options.description: Defer this to the implementer. Risk: engineer ships a frozen Export button, users click it multiple times and receive duplicate downloads.

questions.question: D3 — Pass 2: The plan says 'the existing form skeleton' for initial load. Is this skeleton truly already built, or is it new work that needs a visual spec? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-skeleton>

options.label: Already built — no new spec needed (recommended)
options.description: The skeleton component exists and works today. Plan correctly references it. Implementation task just needs to point to the existing component; no shimmer or gray-box spec required.

options.label: New work — needs visual spec
options.description: The skeleton does not yet exist. The plan needs to describe which elements shimmer (input fields? section headings? the action group?). Adds spec work before implementation can start. (human: ~1h / CC: ~10min)

answers.D3 \u2014 Pass 2: The plan says 'the exi: Already built — no new spec needed (recommended)

questions.question: D4 — Pass 5 / Gap G1: Save button has the same visual weight as Reset, Cancel, and Export. DESIGN.md specifies the fix. Approve adding this implementation task? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-g1-save-style>

options.label: Approve DESIGN.md fix: Save = filled primary (#1d4ed8 + white text), others = ghost (recommended)
options.description: Style Save as the filled primary Button component; Reset, Cancel, Export as neutral ghost variants. Exact tokens from DESIGN.md. Immediately tells users which action is primary. (human: ~1h / CC: ~10min)

options.label: Keep all four buttons equal weight
options.description: Leave all four buttons visually identical. Users must read labels to find Save. Contradicts the DESIGN.md primary/ghost distinction. Not recommended for a primary action page.

options.label: Different visual distinction — size or border only
options.description: Make Save larger or bolder rather than filled. Requires new design work outside DESIGN.md; adds ambiguity. Not recommended when DESIGN.md already specifies the exact solution.

answers.D4 \u2014 Pass 5 / Gap G1: Save button h: Approve DESIGN.md fix: Save = filled primary (#1d4ed8 + white text), others = ghost (recommended)

questions.question: D5 — Pass 5 / Gap G2: Spacing is inconsistent (16px / 24px / 32px). DESIGN.md specifies sections = 32px, field groups = 24px, label-to-input = 8px. The 16px is the offender. Approve normalizing to the DESIGN.md 8px scale? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-g2-spacing>

options.label: Approve DESIGN.md fix: normalize to sections=32px, groups=24px, label=8px (recommended)
options.description: Apply the DESIGN.md 8px base scale. Eliminates the 16px rogue value. Creates consistent vertical rhythm. Implementation task will identify the specific element(s) using 16px. (human: ~1h / CC: ~10min)

options.label: Leave spacing as-is
options.description: Accept the 16px/24px/32px mix. The user will see inconsistent breathing room between elements — professional but not polished. Contradicts DESIGN.md. Not recommended.

answers.D5 \u2014 Pass 5 / Gap G2: Spacing is in: Approve DESIGN.md fix: normalize to sections=32px, groups=24px, label=8px (recommended)

questions.question: D6 — Pass 5 / Gap G3: Error colors. The plan says contrast is ~3:1. But DESIGN.md's tokens (#991b1b on #fef2f2) actually achieve ~7.4:1 — the plan's claim describes the *current wrong implementation*, not the fix. Approve applying DESIGN.md tokens and correcting the contrast claim in the plan? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-g3-error-color>

options.label: Approve: apply DESIGN.md error tokens + correct the contrast claim (recommended)
options.description: Use error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2 with an icon. Update the plan to state the ~3:1 is the current wrong value and the DESIGN.md fix achieves ~7.4:1. Prevents implementers from researching a problem that doesn’t exist in the fixed state. (human: ~1h / CC: ~10min)

options.label: Apply tokens only, leave the plan’s contrast claim unchanged
options.description: Fix the colors but keep the misleading ~3:1 description. Risk: future readers think the DESIGN.md fix still has a contrast problem and add unnecessary workarounds.

Approve: apply DESIGN.md error tokens + correct the contrast claim (recommended)

questions.question: D7 — Pass 5 / Gap G4: Form uses 14px, 16px, and 18px. DESIGN.md specifies two roles: 16px (body/labels/helper text) and 20px (section headings). 14px also violates the universal rule (body text < 16px is prohibited). Approve rationalizing to 16px + 20px only? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-g4-typography>

options.label: Approve DESIGN.md fix: 16px body/labels/helper + 20px headings, eliminate 14px and 18px (recommended)
options.description: Removes the accessibility violation (14px body text) and the intermediate 18px that creates false hierarchy. Implementation task will identify which elements currently use 14px and 18px. Strong two-tier system: 16px for everything readable, 20px for h2 section headings. (human: ~1h / CC: ~10min)

options.label: Keep 14px for helper/secondary text
options.description: Retain 14px for less prominent text (e.g., field hints). Risks: violates body text accessibility rule; creates three-size system instead of two; small text on a form erodes usability. Not recommended.

options.label: Use 18px for section headings instead of 20px
options.description: Compromise: 16px body + 18px headings. Creates weaker section hierarchy than DESIGN.md’s 20px; implementer must override DESIGN.md token. Not recommended when the spec is already clear.

answers.D7 \u2014 Pass 5 / Gap G4: Form uses 14p: Approve DESIGN.md fix: 16px body/labels/helper + 20px headings, eliminate 14px and 18px (recommended)

questions.question: D8 — Pass 5 / Gap G5: Save takes 2-5s with no feedback (frozen page). DESIGN.md specifies the fix exactly. Approve adding the loading indicator? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-g5-motion>

options.label: Approve DESIGN.md fix: inline spinner + “Saving…” inside disabled Save, aria-busy=true, reduced-motion support (recommended)
options.description: Reuses the DESIGN.md established pending-action pattern. Spinner appears beside “Saving…” text inside the Save button; button is disabled while pending; aria-busy=true for screen readers; @media (prefers-reduced-motion) suppresses animation. User sees immediate feedback, never a frozen page. (human: ~2h / CC: ~15min)

options.label: Page-level skeleton or overlay instead
options.description: Show a full-page loading overlay or skeleton while saving. Higher visual weight than a simple button spinner; harder to implement; inconsistent with the DESIGN.md pattern. Overkill for a small form save. Not recommended.

options.label: Toast notification after save instead of spinner during
options.description: Show a toast notification after success rather than in-button feedback during save. Doesn’t solve the frozen-page problem (the user still sees nothing during 2-5s). Not recommended.

answers.D8 \u2014 Pass 5 / Gap G5: Save takes 2-: Approve DESIGN.md fix: inline spinner + “Saving…” inside disabled Save, aria-busy=true, reduced-motion support (recommended)
